columns.description: Cedar-internal row key, `INV-nnnn`, assigned in descending order of total obligations within the candidate set. Stable only within a build; join on `awardee_uei`, never on this.

columns.description: Most frequent recipient state on the contract rows. The FILING address, not necessarily the owner's residence.

columns.description: How the firm entered the register. `TOP400_FLAGGED` — an unattributed awardee in the top 400 by obligations carrying a native self-certification. `PRIOR_OWNER_RULING` — the owner had already ruled it individually Native-owned and the flag route does not reach it. **The second stream is not a footnote: 22 of the 40 prior-ruled firms carry no native self-certification on any contract row**, so the federal flag is a discovery channel with a measured blind spot, not a definition of the population.
columns.name: candidate_basis

columns.description: Prime contract rows in `prime_contracts.csv` for this awardee, all years. Transaction-level for archive years, award-year-vendor aggregate for BGOV years - the two grains are not the same and this count mixes them.
columns.name: n_contract_rows

columns.description: Nominal obligations summed across those rows. Not deflated.
columns.name: total_obligations_usd

columns.description: Earliest fiscal year observed.
columns.name: fy_min

columns.description: Latest fiscal year observed. **Measured 2026-08-26: this is 2022 or earlier on 100% of rows**, because every FY2023-2026 row in `prime_contracts.csv` already carries `attributed_flag = 1` - the archive backfill was seeded from known Native identifiers and is not a full-universe pull. See `temporal_caveat`.
columns.name: fy_max

columns.description: Rank by obligations among all `attributed_flag = 0` awardees. The candidate set is the flagged subset of the top 400.
columns.name: obligations_rank_among_unattributed

columns.description: EVIDENCE FIELD 1 of 4. `YES` on every row by construction: the awardee carries at least one of `reported_8a`, `reported_buy_indian`, `reported_indian_business`, `reported_native_preference` on at least one contract row. **This is the firm asserting its own status to the government.** It carries False Claims Act exposure and is therefore weighty, and it is still self-certification. START_HERE's counter-example: Goldbelt Raven, an ANC subsidiary, certifies `alaskanNativeCorporationOwnedFirm = NO`.
columns.name: sam_self_certification

columns.description: Which of the four flags were ever set, pipe-separated.
columns.name: sam_flags_asserted

columns.description: Contract rows carrying at least one flag.
columns.name: sam_flag_contract_rows

columns.description: `sam_flag_contract_rows / n_contract_rows`. A LOW share is not evidence against the firm: a set-aside is a property of the AWARD and the archive leaves it blank on 56% of transactions (AGENTS.md, 2026-08-08).
columns.name: sam_flag_row_share

columns.description: Most frequent `setaside` strings with counts.
columns.name: sam_setaside_values

columns.description: EVIDENCE FIELD 2 of 4. What the company's OWN website says. One of: `CLAIM_FOUND`, `NO_CLAIM_FOUND`, `SITE_UNREACHABLE`, `NO_SITE_FOUND`, `NOT_CHECKED`. **`NO_CLAIM_FOUND` IS NOT `NOT_NATIVE`.** Many small contractors simply do not advertise ownership. `SITE_UNREACHABLE` covers 500s and timeouts, which are facts about the moment; only 404 and 403 are facts about the object.
columns.name: self_description

columns.description: The VERBATIM SENTENCE from the company's own site stating ownership. This is the unit of evidence and the thing the project owner asked to see. Never paraphrased, never two fragments stitched together. Suppress on any row where `publishable_sentence = N`.
columns.name: self_description_sentence

columns.description: The exact page the sentence was read from.
columns.name: self_description_url

columns.description: When it was retrieved. Pair this with `fy_max` before drawing any conclusion about the contract years.
columns.name: self_description_fetch_date

columns.description: Observed status. `404`/`403` are facts about the object; anything else is a fact about the moment.
columns.name: self_description_http_status

columns.description: What KIND of owner the company's own sentence describes. One of: `INDIVIDUAL_NATIVE`, `TRIBAL_ENTITY`, `ALASKA_NATIVE_CORPORATION`, `NATIVE_HAWAIIAN_ORGANIZATION`, `NATIVE_UNSPECIFIED` (says Native-owned without saying which), `NON_NATIVE_OWNER_NAMED`, or blank.
columns.name: self_description_ownership_kind

columns.description: EVIDENCE FIELD 3 of 4. `FOUND` / `NOT_FOUND` / `NOT_CHECKED`. The only leg in this table that is NOT the firm speaking about itself, and therefore the only one that can carry a row to tier A.
columns.name: third_party

columns.description: One of: `SBA_8A`, `SBA_DSBS`, `TRIBAL_CERTIFYING_BODY`, `TRADE_PRESS`, `COURT_OR_GAO`, `OTHER`.
columns.name: third_party_source_type

columns.description: Verbatim sentence from the third-party source.
columns.name: third_party_sentence

columns.description: Its URL.
columns.name: third_party_url

columns.description: When retrieved.
columns.name: third_party_fetch_date

columns.description: EVIDENCE FIELD 4 of 4. `YES` only where a source names the SPECIFIC tribe or nation. "A citizen of the Cherokee Nation" is `YES`; "Native American owned" is `NO`. The distinction is the whole point of the field - an unnamed claim cannot be checked against a tribal roll and cannot be joined to the entity spine.
columns.name: tribal_affiliation_named

columns.description: The tribe or nation as the source names it. NOT resolved to a `tribe_id`: resolving it would key a dollar off a name, which is the containment defect.
columns.name: tribal_affiliation_name

columns.description: The URL that names the tribe.
columns.name: tribal_affiliation_source

columns.description: The project owner's own standing ruling where one exists. `INDIVIDUAL_NATIVE` or `INDIVIDUAL_NATIVE_NOT_TRIBAL`. **Never overwritten by anything in this table.** A later web pass may add evidence to such a row; it may not change the ruling.
